name: buzzer
description: Buzzer driver supporting both passive (PWM tone control) and active (fixed-frequency) buzzers. Passive mode supports note-based melody playback.

constructor_params.name: pin
constructor_params.description: GPIO pin connected to buzzer signal (must support PWM for passive mode)

constructor_params.name: is_passive
constructor_params.description: True for passive buzzer (PWM tone control). False for active buzzer (fixed tone, on/off only).

constructor_params.name: active_high
constructor_params.description: True: high level triggers sound. False: low level triggers (for some active buzzers).

methods.name: beep
methods.description: Beep `times` times. Each beep lasts `duration` seconds, separated by `interval` seconds.

methods.name: play_note

parameters.name: note
parameters.description: Note name with octave: 'C4', 'D5', 'A3', etc. Empty string '' = silence.

methods.description: Play a musical note. Only works on passive buzzers. Supports major scale notes C, D, E, F, G, A, B at octaves 3-6+.

methods.name: set_tone_freq
methods.description: Set PWM frequency and duty cycle. Passive buzzer only.

methods.name: deinit
methods.description: Release PWM resources and set pin low

class_constants._NOTE_COMMENT: Base frequencies for octave 4. Other octaves computed as freq * 2^(octave-4)

example:
from machine import Pin
from buzzer import Buzzer

# Passive buzzer with melody
bz = Buzzer(Pin(4))
bz.play_note('C4', 0.5)
bz.play_note('E4', 0.5)
bz.play_note('G4', 0.5)

# Active buzzer
bz2 = Buzzer(Pin(4), is_passive=False)
bz2.beep(times=3, duration=0.2)
bz2.deinit()
esp32_notes: NOTE_FREQUENCIES only contains major scale notes (C, D, E, F, G, A, B) — no sharps/flats (#, b)
play_note() silently ignores unsupported note names (prints warning)
PWM default frequency 1000Hz, duty 512 (50%) — adjustable via set_tone_freq()
Passing note='' is a rest (silence for duration seconds)
hardware_notes: Passive buzzers require PWM-capable pin — all GPIO except 34-39 work
Active buzzers only need digital on/off — works on any GPIO
External transistor recommended for high-volume buzzers (passive piezo types)
differences_from_standard_mp: Standard MicroPython requires manual PWM setup. Buzzer abstracts this plus adds note-to-frequency mapping.
Standard PWM can play any frequency. Buzzer adds play_note() with built-in note table.
